title: fix: price MiniMax Turbo at current fal cost
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Set MiniMax H3 Max Turbo cost and customer price to fal’s current promo rates: 480p $0.0125/s, 768p $0.02/s, 1080p $0.04/s; keep `priceMultiplier: 1`. Replaces #15413’s list-price decision.
- Bill from fal’s reported weighted units at the reviewed registry rate. Turbo uses no live pricing lookup; H3 Max retains its existing lookup. Preserve requested-model quotes for fallbacks.
- Pass the billing rate explicitly from the caller, remove unnecessary test changes, and correct the price-sheet comment: public duration × rate need not reproduce a provider-unit-based total.
- Validation: 237 focused tests, Gen/Enter type checks, Biome, and six authenticated local cases passed. Both text-to-video and image-to-video at 480p/768p/1080p matched fal’s actual charges: five seconds used 5/8/16 units and cost $0.0625/$0.10/$0.20. Each proved disconnect/rejoin, identical cached video, one upstream job, one wallet debit, one staging billing event, and no missing-rate warnings.
- Restore published rates through #15555 before the September 30, 2026 promotion ends, including production promotion/deployment. Maintainer accepts switching a few hours early. During that window recorded cost follows configuration and can differ from fal’s actual charge; reconcile afterward. No automatic switch or deployment.

gist.headline: Turbo gets the right price tag
gist.blurb: MiniMax H3 Max Turbo now uses fal’s current promotional rates. The billing ledger reads fal’s weighted units, because video pricing apparently needed one more unit of measurement.
gist.summary: MiniMax H3 Max Turbo now quotes fal’s promotional prices of $0.0125/s at 480p, $0.02/s at 768p, and $0.04/s at 1080p, while billing from fal’s reported weighted units at the configured rate.
gist.impact: A five-second Turbo video at 480p, 768p, or 1080p costs $0.0625, $0.10, or $0.20 respectively; these promotional rates require a manual update before September 30, 2026.
gist.visual_concept: Depict three cozy pixel video screens labeled 480p, 768p, and 1080p, each connected to a small ledger showing its price. Polli, wearing a tiny accountant’s visor, checks the ledger while the Monitor Robot holds the video reels; code-flowers grow around their workspace. The three sizes and matching prices are the visual focus, not a generic sale sign.
